title: How Denmark converts an IB Diploma
note: The Agency's handbook as published, in its own wording, and the source Denmark's pages render from. The machine-readable form the eligibility engine executes is the Recognition Scheme in data/recognition/dk.json: same numbers, named scales, and no assumption that there is only one country. Change the handbook here and change the scheme there, in the same commit.

authority.name: Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen (Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science)
authority.note: Every Danish institution converts IB results using this handbook. Individual university pages are often out of date; this is the source they are all supposed to follow.

importantForTwentySeven: The grade-average conversion table is re-issued every year. The table for a given summer intake is published by 1 March of that year and applies until the end of February the following year. If you are applying for August 2027, check for the table published by 1 March 2027 — the numbers below are the version current as of September 2026 and may shift by a decimal or two.
The single-grade table (used only where a programme sets a minimum grade in a subject) has been stable for years and is far less likely to move.
Subject-level equivalences change rarely. The current table already covers the post-2019 IB mathematics courses.

access.summary: An IB Diploma with 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark, provided you also meet the programme's specific subject requirements.

rules.detail: There is no requirement that every subject be passed with at least 3. A grade of 2 may appear in an IB Diploma, as long as the IB's own conditions for awarding the Diploma were met.
rules.note: This is a genuine and useful difference from what several Danish university pages say. The agency's handbook is the governing source.

rules.situation: DP Course Results / IB Certificate, at least 18 points, minimum grade 3 in all six subjects, at least 3 subjects at HL
rules.givesAccessTo: Academy profession and professional bachelor programmes (through quota 1 and quota 2)
rules.detail: Treated on equal terms with the two-year hf examination without the overbygning extension.

rules.situation: DP Course Results / IB Certificate as above, plus supplementary upper-secondary subjects
rules.detail: The supplement must consist of two successive raises of subject level, at least one of them to A-level. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B-level are enough. Supplementary subjects are taken as hf-enkeltfag, or as a self-study candidate, and are taught in Danish.
rules.note: A retake of the full IB Diploma is the alternative route. GSK cannot be used for this: the Agency states plainly that an IB student cannot use gymnasial supplering to raise their education level. GSK is for somebody whose examination already qualifies them and who is missing a specific subject level — so it is the right tool for a full Diploma holder needing Mathematics A, and the wrong one for Course Results trying to reach a university bachelor. A GSK subject taken to meet a specific requirement for an erhvervsakademi or professionsbachelor programme does stay valid if you later switch to a university bachelor.

rules.situation: DP Course Results under 18 points, or containing any grade of 1 or 2
rules.givesAccessTo: Nothing — not a qualifying examination in Denmark

access.retakeRule: Check the letter at the bottom left of your diploma. D is an original result, R is a retake. If you retook to improve a result that already qualified you, Denmark converts your ORIGINAL result, not the improved one.
access.resultsTiming: IB results are released on 6 July. Danish applications close on 15 March, so you apply before you have your results and ask your IB coordinator to send them directly through the IB's results service (up to six institutions).

gradeAverage.label: IB total points → Danish 7-point grade average
gradeAverage.appliesTo: Graduates up to and including 2019, and from 2023 onwards — which includes everyone sitting the May 2027 session.

legacyTable.label: Graduates of 2020, 2021 and 2022 only — kept for reference

singleGrade.label: Single IB subject grade → Danish 7-point grade
singleGrade.usedFor: Only for programmes that set a minimum grade in a named subject. It is not used to build your average.
singleGrade.rule: Where a subject was completed at several levels, the highest grade at or above the required level is used. A grade at a level below the one required does not count at all.

subjectLevels.label: IB subject and level → Danish subject level
subjectLevels.note: Prepared by the Danish Ministry of Children and Education. Danish levels are A (highest), B and C — they are levels of study, not grades.

ib: English A Literature HL or SL (from 2013)
English A Language and Literature HL or SL (from 2013)

map.warning: The handbook lists no IB equivalent for Geoscience A. If a programme requires Geoscience A you will normally need a Danish supplementary course.

map.note: The subject may appear as History Europe, History Asia and so on depending on where it was taken.

specialCases.subject: Global Politics
specialCases.verdict: No fixed equivalence. Each institution decides.
specialCases.detail: Global Politics is 150 hours at SL and 240 at HL. Danish Social Studies (samfundsfag) B covers sociology, economics, politics and method; A adds international politics. Global Politics goes far deeper into international politics than Danish Social Studies A, but does not cover the sociology and economics that the Danish subject includes. Institutions decide case by case whether it meets Social Studies C, B or A — sometimes only in combination with another social science subject.
specialCases.advice: If a programme asks for Social Studies B and you took Global Politics, write to the admissions office before 15 March and ask for a written assessment. Do not assume it counts.

specialCases.subject: Theory of Knowledge (TOK)
specialCases.detail: TOK does not correspond to any subject in the Danish upper secondary system. Depending on what you covered, it may earn credit towards small parts of certain Danish subjects, but it does not satisfy a subject requirement.

specialCases.subject: Danish ab initio
specialCases.verdict: Equivalent to nothing in the Danish-as-a-second-language ladder.
specialCases.detail: Danish ab initio, Danish B HL and Danish B SL are foreign-language subjects aimed at listening, speaking, reading and writing Danish. Whether Danish ab initio or Danish B HL can replace Danish A as the Danish-language requirement is left to each institution.

specialCases.subject: Geoscience A (Geovidenskab A)
specialCases.detail: The handbook explicitly leaves the IB column blank for Geoscience A. IB Geography HL is not automatically accepted; the agency publishes a separate note comparing the two.

danishLanguage.summary: Most Danish bachelor programmes are taught in Danish, and for those you must document Danish at A level.
routes: Danish A1 HL / Danish A Literature HL — meets Danish A.
Danish A1 SL / Danish A Literature SL — normally accepted for Danish A at university, because it sits above the Studieprøven test.
Studieprøven i dansk — the national Danish language test for higher education. Universities may allow it in place of Danish A for applicants with a non-Nordic qualification.
Danish B HL or Danish ab initio — decided institution by institution. Ask in writing.
danishLanguage.note: Studieprøven is not an upper-secondary subject, so it can never be used to meet a subject grade requirement — only the language requirement.
